🇮🇹 Ha ancora senso parlare di borse da uomo?
Spoiler: no. Una borsa è una borsa. 🖤

Perché nel 2025 sono sempre di più i gentlemen — di ogni generazione, su ogni red carpet — che hanno trovato nelle It-Bag il pezzo mancante del proprio stile. Da A$AP Rocky a Timothée Chalamet, da Jacob Elordi a Harry Styles: nessuno di loro si è fermato a chiedersi se fosse "da uomo". L'hanno presa, l'hanno indossata e stavano divinamente.

I brand lo sanno. Gli stylist che fanno a gara per accaparrarsi pezzi d'archivio lo sanno. E a giudicare dai look in circolazione, la distinzione di genere negli accessori è un concetto che ha già fatto il suo tempo.

Dai modelli minimal di @therow alle creazioni leggendarie di @hermes: l'uomo contemporaneo ha già scelto. Il resto è solo rumore. 👜

🇬🇧 Does it still make sense to talk about men's bags?
Spoiler: no. A bag is a bag. 🖤

Because in 2025, more and more gentlemen—of every generation, on every red carpet—have found the missing piece of their style in It-Bags. From A$AP Rocky to Timothée Chalamet, from Jacob Elordi to Harry Styles: none of them stopped to ask if it was "for men." They took it, wore it, and looked divine.

Brands know it. Stylists competing to snap up archive pieces know it. And judging by the looks currently circulating, gender distinction in accessories is a concept that has already had its day.

From @therow's minimal designs to @hermes' legendary creations: the contemporary man has already made his choice. The rest is just noise. 👜

THE MEN’S ACCESSORY EDIT | KENG HARIT MAKES THE CASE FOR THE CROSSBODY

Sometimes the detail that changes an outfit is also the smallest one.

In a recent Saint Laurent-tagged style moment, Keng Harit takes one of menswear’s most familiar combinations, a white shirt and faded denim, and gives it considerably more character through the accessories.

He starts the look off with something simple.

A relaxed white shirt is layered over black at the collar and cuffs. Faded jeans fall into a slightly flared silhouette, while a brown leather belt and square-toe shoes bring warmth to the otherwise restrained palette.

Then comes the black Saint Laurent crossbody bag.

Small, structured and worn close to the body, it does more than provide somewhere to carry the essentials. Against the softness of the shirt and worn-in denim, the polished leather introduces another texture and gives the entire look a sharper point of focus.

That contrast is what makes the styling work.

Relaxed denim. Crisp shirting. Polished leather.

Nothing competes for attention, yet every element contributes something different.

Keng has also made bags a recurring part of his personal style, pairing different shapes with everything from casual separates to more directional looks, a useful reminder that the men's bag has moved far beyond pure practicality.

Here, the crossbody functions much like the belt or shoes: it finishes the outfit rather than simply accompanying it.

And there is a broader style lesson worth taking from the look.

When the clothes are simple, adding more clothing isn't always the answer.

Sometimes what an outfit needs is one accessory with enough structure, texture or personality to pull everything together.

Keng fans, which detail gets your vote in this look,the relaxed denim, the sharp white shirt, or the Saint Laurent bag?

By day, it looks like a quietly distinctive Louis Vuitton Speedy. Turn down the lights, and the story changes completely.

Fourth Nattawat Jirochtikul puts the spotlight on Louis Vuitton’s Monogram Firefly Speedy P9, pairing the bag with a relaxed mix of a distressed brown jacket, crisp white shirt, black tie and easy cream trousers.

But the accessory is where things get unexpected.

Louis Vuitton has screen-printed the Monogram using phosphorescent ink, allowing the pattern to absorb light and later illuminate in the dark with a luminous glow. It is a playful technical update to one of the house’s most recognizable bag silhouettes and part of Louis Vuitton’s Fall-Winter 2026 story.

Fourth’s styling also makes a useful menswear point: a statement bag does not always need an equally statement-heavy outfit. Against neutral brown, cream, black and white, the Speedy becomes the detail that changes the entire look.

And after dark? It quite literally does.
